title: Commissioners' Meeting 06/22/26
tldr: After a public hearing, the Board unanimously adopted the FY 2027 budget, with an $82.5 million General Fund and no property tax increase. It renewed the Veterans' History Museum of the Carolinas lease for two years at the current rate and approved $2,184,218 from Education Capital Fund balance for a new standardized secure vestibule at every school. It also approved FY 2027 nonprofit grant contracts and heard a clean FY 2025 audit opinion. After a closed session, the Board directed a certified letter to Connestee Fire Rescue about answering audit questions, for the purpose of negotiating a contract revision and/or a 90-day termination.

keyVotes.background: The consent agenda covered: minutes, including sealed closed session minutes; tax discovery, release and settlement reports for May and June 1-22, 2026; a proclamation naming July Park and Recreation Month; a letter supporting AdventHealth's Certificate of Need application for 92 acute care beds in Weaverville; the FY 2027 Home and Community Care Block Grant plan; and the FY 2027 Juvenile Crime Prevention Council funding plan. It also included an $8,500 amendment to the FY 2025 audit contract with Martin Starnes & Associates, transfer of the vacant CARE Coalition Director position to the NC Public Health Alliance Staffing Agency, moving the Health Department training day to September 30, 2026, and out-of-state travel for the IT Director to the NACo Annual Conference.

keyVotes.description: Reappointed seven members to the Juvenile Crime Prevention Council
keyVotes.background: The terms of Cynthiana Cain, Sarah Holden, Jennifer Galloway, Jake Dalton, April Cameron, Chase Lance and Dr. Brian Weaver expire at the end of June. All were eligible and willing to serve again in statutory roles. Staff continues recruiting for several vacancies.

keyVotes.description: Tabled the recommended appointment of Kay Argroves to the Regional Council on Aging
keyVotes.background: LeeAnne Tucker of the Land of Sky Area Agency on Aging recommended Ms. Argroves for a Community Member seat that would also serve as Alternate Senior Tar Heel Delegate. There are two vacancies on the council.
keyVotes.discussion: Chairwoman McCall recommended tabling because Ms. Argroves does not meet the Citizen Advisory Council Policy requirements to live in the County full-time and be registered to vote there.

keyVotes.description: Appointed Jason Davis to the North Transylvania Fire Rescue Relief Fund Board
keyVotes.background: County appointee Matthew Petty resigned from the Relief Fund Board. The North Transylvania Fire Rescue Board of Directors selected Jason Davis to fill the vacancy and recommended his appointment.

keyVotes.description: Adopted the FY 2027 budget: $82.5 million General Fund, no property tax increase
keyVotes.background: The County Manager presented the recommended budget: a $82.5 million General Fund, up 1.47% with no tax increase, and a 2.7% overall increase for outside agencies. It fully funds the Board of Education and Blue Ridge Community College requests and uses fund balance to cover possible state and federal cost shifts. It also includes a $4.1 million Solid Waste fund with a $720,000 General Fund subsidy and fire district spending just under $7 million with no fire tax increase. A public hearing was held earlier in the meeting.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner Chapman said the budget process has been transparent, supported the no-tax-increase budget and said counties would need to reprioritize if property tax limits are approved. Commissioner Chappell said budgeting is year-round, cited uncertainty from the state not having adopted a budget, urged discussion of a local sales tax referendum and credited last year's revaluation for the County's position. Commissioner Dalton cited coming pressures from SNAP administration, teacher salaries and Medicaid Hold Harmless. Commissioner McKelvey supported a future sales tax initiative and noted the budget does not address Parks and Recreation investment or a long-term Solid Waste solution. Chairwoman McCall said more than 90% of the budget is mandated services and that future budgets may be harder.

keyVotes.description: Renewed the Veterans' History Museum of the Carolinas lease for two years at the current rate
keyVotes.background: The lease of the former Administration Building expires June 30, 2026. The rate has been $625 per month (about $2 per square foot, including utilities) for eight years, against an estimated $12 per square foot break-even and a downtown market rate of $18 to $26. One HVAC unit has failed: replacement is estimated at $20,000, a compressor repair at about $5,000 and mini-splits at $15,000. Under the lease the museum is responsible for HVAC, and the arrangement will reach the 10-year statutory threshold for competitive procedures within about two years.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner Chapman disclosed he no longer serves on the museum's board and has no conflict. He said the museum likely cannot afford a market rate and that by the end of a two-year term the future of the existing courthouse should be clearer. Chairwoman McCall asked whether the motion would leave HVAC responsibility with the museum, and Commissioner Chapman replied that under the existing lease it remains with the museum; she also asked about the lower-cost HVAC option. Commissioner Chappell asked about the mini-split cost, suggested requiring an RFP for courthouse use within the two-year period and said he did not support investing in a new HVAC system. Commissioner McKelvey noted the rate has not changed while costs rose and asked for the break-even figure.

keyVotes.description: Approved FY 2027 nonprofit funding contracts ($100,000 allocation)
keyVotes.background: Budget and Management Analyst Jennifer Wright reported 30 applications requesting $250,000 for $100,000 in available funds. The applications were scored by a committee that included Commissioners McKelvey and Chappell. Awards went to human services organizations and culture and recreation organizations, including $10,000 to Housing Assistance Corporation with another $10,000 held in reserve. No recusals were recorded.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner Chapman asked whether funded nonprofits must report on progress. Ms. Wright said updates and year-end reports are required, and the Manager added that all recipients sign contracts. Commissioner Chappell thanked the review committee and said the updated rating process made reviews more consistent.

keyVotes.description: Directed that the reserved $10,000 for Housing Assistance Corporation return to the Board for approval when requested
keyVotes.background: An additional $10,000 in designated housing funds for Housing Assistance Corporation is held in reserve pending a mid-year spending report. Ms. Wright asked whether the Board wanted that release to come back for approval.

keyVotes.description: Approved $2,184,218 from Education Capital Fund balance for a standardized secure vestibule at every school, plus authority to move up to 5% between project scopes
keyVotes.background: The new vestibule standard costs an estimated $5.4 million beyond the original scopes. It is funded by $3.2 million in reallocated bond project savings and $2,184,218 in Education Capital Fund balance, and the amendment also shifts work toward the Rosman Area Schools scope. Both the Education Capital Subcommittee and the Board of Education recommended approval. The 5% transfer authority requires agreement of the County Manager and Superintendent and cannot raise the overall budget, and completion remains targeted for the end of 2028.
keyVotes.discussion: Commissioner Chappell said no approved projects are removed and security improvements are added. Commissioner Chapman asked whether School Resource Officer locations were considered, and Dr. Fletcher said they were. Commissioner Dalton asked about Rosman High and Middle entrances and was told they will be combined into one. Chairwoman McCall sought clarification on whether the retaining wall project would still be completed and whether the fund balance money was already available; the County Manager confirmed the project will proceed under County management and that the funds are cash fund balance restricted for educational capital. Commissioner McKelvey noted $3.2 million in savings reduced the request to about $2.1 million.

keyVotes.description: Entered closed session to protect confidential information and consult the County Attorney
keyVotes.background: The closed session was held under N.C.G.S. 143-318.11(a)(1) and (a)(3), after a 10-minute recess. It began at 8:54 p.m.
The Board consulted with the County Attorney and staff on a confidential matter and left closed session at 9:54 p.m.
The minutes are sealed until opening them would not frustrate the purpose of the closed session.

keyVotes.description: Directed a certified letter to Connestee Fire Rescue on answering audit questions, toward a contract revision and/or 90-day termination
keyVotes.background: This followed direction given in closed session. The County Attorney and staff are to send the letter to the Chief, Board Chair and all Board Members of Connestee Fire Rescue.

topics.text: Said a great deal of school capital work had been completed since the interlocal agreement and that projects coming in under budget allowed additional improvements to be considered.
Recommended tabling the Regional Council on Aging appointment because the candidate did not meet the County's full-time residency and voter registration requirements.
Asked members to review the staff groupings of NCACC legislative goals and be ready to approve them at the July 13 meeting.
Noted that more than 90% of the County budget is mandated services and said FY 2027 may be one of the easier budget cycles compared with future years.
Asked whether the museum lease motion left HVAC responsibility with the museum and asked for clarification on the lower-cost HVAC option.
Reported she had asked state legislators to combine the new courthouse and existing courthouse renovation requests into one court facilities funding request.
Said a multi-tenant approach may be most practical for the existing courthouse, supported an RFP and described the Veterans' History Museum as a valuable community asset.
Sought clarification on whether the Rosman High School retaining wall project would still be completed and whether the $2.1 million education capital fund balance was already available.
Said serving on the nonprofit funding review committee was among the most challenging committee work she had done.
Asked whether General Fund support beyond the $720,000 Solid Waste subsidy was recommended for other agencies.
Said a transparent audit process helps build public trust in how taxpayer dollars are managed.
Asked whether school construction would affect students when classes resume in August.
Responded to public hearing comments by saying the budget process is transparent, with posted agendas, open meetings and online recordings.
Supported the no-tax-increase budget and said counties would need to reprioritize if a property tax limitation amendment is approved.
Praised the NCACC legislative goals process and recognized NCACC Executive Director Kevin Leonard.
Disclosed he no longer serves on the Veterans' History Museum board and has no conflict of interest.
Said the museum likely cannot afford a market-rate lease, cited its value to veterans and visitors and recommended a two-year renewal.
Asked whether funded nonprofits must provide progress reports and said nonprofit funding comes with accountability.
Asked whether School Resource Officer locations were considered in the secure vestibule design.
Recognized the County Manager's new NC City-County Management Association role and thanked the Superintendent for well-received principal assignments.
Urged candidates in attendance and future officials to keep advocating directly with state legislators.
Thanked the auditors for responding to the County's RFP and urged continued advocacy with the General Assembly about the shrinking number of governmental audit firms.
Asked whether further changes to Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) rules were expected.
Highlighted that all first-phase school bond projects are projected to be complete by the end of 2028.
Said budgeting is a year-round process and noted the state's lack of an adopted budget creates uncertainty for counties.
Emphasized economic development, workforce development and support for Blue Ridge Community College.
Encouraged continued discussion of a local sales tax referendum and said last year's revaluation decision strengthened the County's finances.
Asked about the mini-split HVAC cost and said he did not support investing in a new HVAC system for the former Administration Building.
Encouraged an RFP for the existing courthouse that allows partnerships or multiple tenants, and suggested requiring it be issued within the two-year lease period.
Thanked the nonprofit review committee and said the updated rating process made reviews more consistent.
Supported the secure vestibule budget amendment, saying it adds security without removing approved projects.
Asked whether the replacement school roofs would have enough pitch for proper drainage.
Cited possible state-driven cost pressures from SNAP administration, teacher salaries and Medicaid Hold Harmless requirements.
Supported continued advocacy for a different property tax rate for non-resident property owners.
Urged changes to the state economic tier system, saying Tier 3 does not reflect Transylvania County's conditions.
Said he would be absent July 13 and wanted his legislative goal priorities on the record, otherwise supporting the draft goals.
Asked whether Rosman High and Middle Schools would have separate or combined secure entrances.
Noted many school projects are coming in under budget and asked when the security vestibule designs would be available.
Encouraged discussion of a future sales tax initiative so visitors help relieve local property taxpayers.
Raised concerns about unfunded mandates and the coming compensation study and stressed competitive wages.
Said the budget does not include more Parks and Recreation investment or a long-term Solid Waste solution.
Noted the museum lease rate has not changed in eight years while County costs rose, and asked for the break-even cost.
Noted $3.2 million in project savings reduced the $5.4 million vestibule cost to about $2.1 million in new funding.

publicComments.speaker: Owen Carson
publicComments.summary: At the budget public hearing, thanked the Board and staff and commended the County's long-range capital planning. He suggested a public-facing financial roadmap summarizing major future obligations such as school construction, bonds, courthouse, solid waste and state and federal funding changes.

publicComments.speaker: Doug Powell
publicComments.summary: Encouraged reflection on the Declaration of Independence before Independence Day. He spoke about its references to God and individual rights and urged local governments to acknowledge the nation's religious and historical foundations.

publicComments.speaker: Chuck Gilmore
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about a November ballot constitutional amendment limiting property tax increases. He urged the Board to educate residents on its potential impacts.

publicComments.speaker: David Morrow
publicComments.summary: Speaking for the Veterans History Museum of the Carolinas, thanked the Board for the two-year lease extension. He asked that the museum be involved in HVAC discussions and asked about the timeline, including whether work could be done before July 4.

publicComments.speaker: Ashley Hart
publicComments.summary: Thanked the Board for extending the museum lease. She raised concerns about a public records request she submitted and asked the County to consider confirming receipt of such requests.

followUps.description: Bring the reserved additional $10,000 in designated housing funds for Housing Assistance Corporation back to the Board for approval when requested.

During the two-year Veterans' History Museum lease extension, evaluate long-term options for the museum and the future use of the existing courthouse and former Administration Building, including potential leasing arrangements.

Send a certified letter to Connestee Fire Rescue's Chief, Board Chair and Board Members about answering audit questions, for the purpose of negotiating a contract revision and/or a 90-day termination.
followUps.resolution: Staff met twice with Connestee Fire Rescue to work out fiscal controls and revised payment terms. The Board approved parameters for a contract amendment requiring monthly documented reimbursement, with the formal amendment due back September 28, 2026.

followUps.description: Address offsite sediment migration from the landfill cell expansion with NCDEQ, the contractor and the engineer, including water testing. Expansion completion is estimated in September.
followUps.resolution: The County Manager reported that the landfill cell expansion remains on schedule for completion by the end of September. Staff is working with DEQ, the contractor and the engineer on several stormwater-related issues.

followUps.description: Present Hurricane Helene streambank restoration projects to the Board for consideration once they are ready for approval.
followUps.resolution: On the consent agenda, the Board approved using up to $25,000 in Soil & Water special project funds to supplement EWP engineering costs for four Helene streambank restoration projects.

followUps.description: Investigate reports of dogs at large possibly attacking animals and take appropriate action if they are owned.
